questions.q: Which module family includes the General Ledger, Accounts Payable, and Accounts Receivable?
options: Financials
Supply Chain Management
Procurement
HCM
questions.explain: Financials is the accounting core, covering GL, AP, AR, Cash Management, Fixed Assets, Expenses, and Subledger Accounting.

questions.q: What is 'master data' in the context of ERP integration?
options: The transaction history for the current fiscal year only
Shared reference records, like a supplier or customer, used consistently across modules
A password-protected administrative module
Data that only IT staff are allowed to view
questions.explain: Master data (suppliers, customers, employees, and similar records) is shared across modules so each one doesn't keep its own out-of-sync copy.

questions.q: In the expense report example, what determines who approves an employee's expense report?
options: The amount of the expense only
A random assignment by the system
The employee's manager, as recorded in HCM
The Procurement module's supplier list
questions.explain: HCM holds the employee record, including their manager, which Expenses uses to route the approval.

questions.q: Which module family would Manufacturing and Planning belong to?
options: Financials
HCM
Procurement
Supply Chain Management
questions.explain: Supply Chain Management covers Inventory, Order Management, Manufacturing, and Planning.

questions.q: Why does the lesson argue a Financials consultant should understand the surrounding modules, even if Financials is their specialty?
options: Because support issues often trace back to a dependency in another module, like a missing receipt or an HCM approval routing issue
Because Oracle requires certification in every module
Because Financials cannot function without Procurement being installed
Because job titles always combine all four module families
questions.explain: A ticket like 'this invoice won't post' or 'this expense report is stuck' often depends on something in Supply Chain or HCM, not Financials itself.
